interest: This document provides valuable insight into pre-World War II Japanese intelligence gathering and maritime presence in the Indian Ocean, specifically around British Ceylon. It reflects how American consular officials and British colonial authorities monitored suspected espionage and subversive operations potentially masked as illicit fishing activities, highlighting early vigilance over Japanese naval and reconnaissance activities along vital sea lanes.
overview: This file consists of the State Department's 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.20246C, titled 'Military Activities of Japan in Ceylon Including Gathering of Information. Espionage. Propaganda.' Dating from 1936, it records incoming consular despatches from American Consul Robert L. Buell in Colombo concerning suspected Japanese subversive activities and intelligence operations in Ceylon. The indexed entries specifically highlight ongoing surveillance of the situation and the apprehension of Japanese poachers operating aboard the vessel Taikya Maru with five sampans, while noting that another motorboat, the Nagusin Maru, eluded capture.

subfiles.about: A Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing despatches from the American Consulate in Colombo regarding Japanese subversive operations and poaching in Ceylon.
subfiles.summary: This single-page index sheet catalogues despatches received under decimal file 894.20246C regarding Japanese military and intelligence activities in Ceylon during 1936. It records reports forwarded by American Consul Robert L. Buell in Colombo, specifically despatches No. 360 and No. 454. The purport summarizes reports of Japanese subversive activities under consular observation, as well as the apprehension of Japanese poachers on the vessel Taikya Maru and five sampans, noting that the motorboat Nagusin Maru escaped.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Japanese Military Activities in Ceylon
